Move Alaska, Hawaii and Puerto Rico below the contiguous United States

Source: R/shift_noncontiguous.R
shift_noncontiguous.Rd

Rescales Alaska, Hawaii and Puerto Rico and places them below the contiguous United States, so a national map shows all of them at a readable size. Features elsewhere are only transformed to NAD83 / Conus Albers (EPSG:5070).

Usage

shift_noncontiguous(x)

Arguments

x

An sf or sfc object with a coordinate reference system.

Value

x in EPSG:5070, with features in Alaska, Hawaii and Puerto Rico moved and rescaled.

Details

Each feature that falls in or within 100 km of Alaska, Hawaii or Puerto Rico (as drawn in UNOS_regions_sf) is projected to a coordinate reference system suited to that area, rescaled about the area's centroid and moved to a fixed position below the contiguous states. Alaska is drawn at half size, Hawaii at 1.5 times and Puerto Rico at 2.5 times. The same move applies to every layer, so points (such as transplant_centers_sf or the layer from get_hrsa_transplant_centers()) land in the right place on shifted polygons.

Shifted coordinates are positions on a map, not locations: use the result for drawing only, never for spatial joins, distances or areas. Shift state-level or point data before dissolving it into regions, since a feature that spans both the contiguous states and one of these areas is moved as a whole.

The layout follows the "below" layout of tigris::shift_geometry(), which needs an internet connection; this function uses the boundaries bundled with sRtr and works offline.

See also

get_hrsa_optn_regions() with noncontiguous = "shift".

Examples

if (requireNamespace("sf", quietly = TRUE)) {
  shifted <- shift_noncontiguous(UNOS_regions_sf)
  plot(sf::st_geometry(shifted))
  plot(
    sf::st_geometry(shift_noncontiguous(transplant_centers_sf)),
    add = TRUE, pch = 16, cex = 0.4
  )
}
#> Error in .srtr_shift_layout(): `UNOS_regions_sf` has no boundary for "Alaska", "Hawaii", and "Puerto
#> Rico".
